tokens: verbal noun (root of 自殺する)
verb linking the quote to のは

items.jp: 彼らは雨が止むまでポーチで待った。

translation.pt-BR: Eles esperaram na varanda até a chuva parar.
translation.en: They waited on the porch until it stopped raining.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 雨 ('the rain') as the one who performs the action of 止む ('to stop'), within the subordinate clause.
tokens: verb of the subordinate time clause

items.jp: 今日はちょっと頭が痛いの。

translation.pt-BR: Hoje estou com um pouco de dor de cabeça.
translation.en: I have a slight headache today.

items.label: marks the subject that feels the pain (body part)
items.explanation: が marks 頭 as what hurts, in the pattern 〜が痛い ('the head is what hurts').

items.jp: 彼らの時間の多くがアルバイトに使われる。

translation.pt-BR: Boa parte do tempo deles é gasta em bicos.
translation.en: A lot of their time is spent on part-time jobs.

items.label: subject marker
items.explanation: が marks 多く as the subject of the passive: it is 'the greater part' that is spent. With the passive voice, what undergoes the action usually comes with が.

items.jp: 彼は名前を覚えるのが下手だ。

translation.pt-BR: Ele é ruim de gravar nomes.
translation.en: He is weak on names.

items.label: subject marker (in the のが下手 pattern)
items.explanation: が marks that 'act' as that which the person is bad at. In the pattern 〜のが下手, the ability (or lack thereof) always comes with が, not を.

items.jp: 電話したけど留守でした

translation.pt-BR: Liguei, mas não tinha ninguém em casa.
translation.en: I called, but no one was home.

items.label: adversative conjunction 'but'
items.explanation: けど links the two clauses with contrast: 'I called, but (she wasn't there)'. It is the colloquial version of けれど(も).
tokens: object/root of the compound verb (電話する)

items.jp: 値段は一緒だけど、質がいいですよ。

translation.pt-BR: O preço é o mesmo, mas a qualidade é melhor.
translation.en: The price is the same, but the quality is better.

items.label: adversative conjunction ('but')
items.explanation: けど fecha 値段は一緒だ e vira a frase para o contraste: o preço não muda, o que muda é a qualidade.

items.jp: そうかもしれないけど、たぶん違う。

translation.pt-BR: Pode ser que sim, mas provavelmente não é.
translation.en: That could be true, but I don't really think so.

items.label: conjunction 'but' (informal)
items.explanation: けど links the two clauses with contrast; it is the colloquial version of けれども ('but, however').
tokens: adverb (support of かもしれない)

items.jp: 部活のかけもち、大変だと思うけどがんばれよ。

translation.pt-BR: Fazer dois clubes ao mesmo tempo deve ser puxado, mas força aí!
translation.en: I'm sure it's tough taking part in the activities of two clubs, but good luck!

items.label: adversative conjunction ('but')
items.explanation: けど liga o reconhecimento de que é difícil ao incentivo que vem logo depois.

items.jp: 高いけれど、とても便利だ

translation.pt-BR: É caro, mas é muito prático.
translation.en: It's expensive, but it's very practical.

items.label: contrastive conjunction ('but/although')
items.explanation: けれど links the two clauses with an adversative sense: it concedes that it is expensive, but opposes the advantage of being practical. Being an い-adjective, 高い connects to けれど without needing だ.

items.jp: 勉強したけれど、テストは難しかった

translation.pt-BR: Estudei, mas a prova estava difícil.
translation.en: I studied, but the test was hard.

items.label: concessive conjunction ('but, however')
items.explanation: けれど links the two clauses marking contrast: studied, but even so the test was hard. Here it appears right after the past-tense verb 勉強した.
tokens: nominal stem of the compound verb
main verb (part of 勉強する)

items.jp: 今日は疲れたって感じ

translation.pt-BR: Hoje foi aquela sensação de cansaço, sabe?
translation.en: Today had that tired feeling to it, you know?

items.label: casual quotative particle (って) within 〜って感じ
items.explanation: って (colloquial form of と) quotes 疲れた and links it to 感じ, forming 〜って感じ ("the feeling was one of tiredness"). It is the hallmark of this informal expression.

items.jp: 彼は忙しいって

translation.pt-BR: Ele disse que está ocupado.
translation.en: He said he's busy.

items.label: colloquial quotation / hearsay
items.explanation: って at the end relays what he said or what was heard; it attaches directly to the い-adjective 忙しい without a copula.

items.jp: この店はおしゃれって感じだね

translation.pt-BR: Essa loja tem uma cara meio chique, né?
translation.en: This store has a kind of fancy look to it, doesn't it?

items.label: quotative particle (casual)
items.explanation: って quotes おしゃれ as the content of the impression; it is the informal version of という/と before 感じ.

items.jp: あの映画はちょっと怖いって感じだった

translation.pt-BR: Aquele filme deu uma sensação meio assustadora.
translation.en: That movie gave off a kind of scary feeling.

items.label: casual quotative particle (って) within 〜って感じ
items.explanation: って is the colloquial version of と and here quotes the impression ちょっと怖い, linking it to 感じ. It is the heart of the 〜って感じ construction ("it gave a sort of scary feeling").

items.jp: ここに残るって決めたんだ。

translation.pt-BR: Decidi ficar aqui.
translation.en: I've decided to stay here.

items.label: colloquial marker of quotation/content (= と/という)
items.explanation: って packages 'ここに残る' (to stay here) as the content of what was decided by 決めた; it is the spoken/casual version of と.
tokens: auxiliary (copula だ of the explanatory structure んだ)

items.jp: 台所って、お手伝いがいる？

translation.pt-BR: Na cozinha, precisa de ajuda?
translation.en: Do you need help in the kitchen?

items.label: informal topic marker
items.explanation: って is the colloquial version of は/というのは: it introduces 台所 as the theme ('the kitchen, huh? / as for the kitchen').

items.jp: 仕事、探してるんだって？

translation.pt-BR: Soube que você está procurando emprego, é verdade?
translation.en: I heard that you're looking for a job.

items.label: reported-speech marker (I heard that)
items.explanation: って reports information heard from others; with んだ it forms んだって, and with question intonation it seeks to confirm what was heard.

items.jp: まだ決めてないんだって。

translation.pt-BR: Disseram que ela ainda não decidiu.
translation.en: She hasn't decided yet.

items.label: reported-speech marker (I heard that)
items.explanation: って reports information heard from others; with んだ it forms んだって ('they said that / from what I heard').

items.jp: 幸せって何だっけ？

translation.pt-BR: O que mesmo é a felicidade?
translation.en: What is happiness?

items.label: topic particle (colloquial)
items.explanation: って here introduces 幸せ as the topic of the utterance, a colloquial equivalent of というのは/は: 'this thing called happiness'
